etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Anglo-Norman resigner, Middle French resigner, and its source, Latin resignāre (“to unseal, annul, assign, resign”), from re- + signāre (“to seal, stamp”). Piecewise doublet of re-sign.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To give up; to relinquish ownership of. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1603, Michel de Montaigne, chapter 39, in John Florio, transl., The Essayes […], book I, London:  […]  Val[entine] Simmes for Edward Blount […], →OCLC:
quote.text: And if the perfection of well-speaking might bring any glorie sutable unto a great personage, Scipio and Lelius would never have resigned the honour of their Comedies […] unto an Affrican servant […].

definitions.definition: (transitive) To hand over (something to someone), place into the care or control of another.
(transitive or intransitive) To voluntarily leave (a job or position), in particular a hard-fought position of high status. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1974 August 8, Richard Nixon, 2:30 from the start, in Richard Nixon's resignation speech‎[1], CBSN:
quote.text: To continue to fight through the months ahead for my personal vindication would almost totally absorb the time and attention of both the President and the Congress in a period when our entire focus should be on the great issues of peace abroad and prosperity without inflation at home. Therefore, I shall resign the Presidency effective at noon tomorrow. Vice President Ford will be sworn in as President at that hour in this office.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To submit passively; to give up as hopeless or inevitable. [from 15th c.]

quote.citation: 1996, Robin Buss, The Count of Monte Cristo, translation of, Alexandre Dumas, Le Comte de Monte-Cristo, 2003 Penguin edition, →ISBN, page 394 [2]:
quote.text: Here is a man who was resigned to his fate, who was walking to the scaffold and about to die like a coward, that's true, but at least he was about to die without resisting and without recrimination. Do you know what gave him that much strength? Do you know what consoled him? Do you know what resigned him to his fate?

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From re- +‎ sign.

quote.citation: 2020, Kevin McCarthy, mutt 2.0.0 released, mutt-announce mailing list, November 7 2020
quote.text: Lastly, a note that I have resigned my GPG key to extend the expiration date.
